item.title: Jesse Lingard forced to train alone at Corinthians after suffering two fractured ribs as former Man Utd midfielder undergoes 'intensive recovery'
item.description: Corinthians v Internacional - Brasileirao 2026 - Getty Images Sport Former Manchester United playmaker Jesse Lingard has been ordered to work away from his Corinthians team-mates over the coming days after sustaining rib injuries in Brazil. The 33-year-old attacking midfielder is currently undergoing close daily monitoring by club doctors as he battles to regain full fitness for their survival push. Englishman suffers painful rib injury Corinthians announced on Tuesday afternoon that their English playmaker sustained minor fractures to his sixth and seventh ribs . Despite the knock, the former England international was already ruled out of Friday night's Brasileirao home clash against Mirassol through suspension after collecting his third yellow card. Consequently, the veteran will maintain his conditioning away from the main group while receiving targeted treatment from the club's medical staff. Club statement outlines recovery plan Having arrived in Sao Paulo in early March on a deal running until December 2026 with the option of a further 12 months, Lingard has become a regular fixture in South America. Across the current campaign, he has registered one assist in 19 Brazilian Serie A appearances alongside one goal in eight Copa Libertadores outings and another strike across four Copa do Brasil games. Detailing the injury setback on Tuesday, an official Corinthians statement read: "Forward Jesse Lingard suffered minor fractures to his sixth and seventh ribs. The player will train normally in the coming days, but separately. The number 77 has already begun intensive recovery treatment and the Corinthians Medical Department will reassess him daily to clear him to train with the group." Treatment room crowded in Brazil Lingard is the latest high-profile casualty at a crucial stage of the season for newly appointed head coach Clarence Seedorf , whose squad has been hit hard by fitness issues. Former United team-mate Memphis Depay is currently sidelined with oedema in his right thigh, while midfielder Raniele is nursing a sprained right knee and former Arsenal centre-back Gabriel Paulista is out with a left leg adductor strain. In addition to those muscular and joint problems, attacking duo Zakaria Labyad and Kayke remain unavailable as they continue their respective rehabilitations from knee surgery. Relegation dogfight awaits returning playmaker Sitting 18th in the standings on 33 points after 32 games, Seedorf's struggling side trail 16th-placed Internacional by two points in the battle to escape the drop zone. While his team-mates host Mirassol on Friday without him, Lingard will aim to return from injury and suspension for the crucial derby at Sao Paulo on November 4. A home meeting with Botafogo then follows in their final six-game survival run-in.

item.title: Why Hurts played with blood clot and what it means for NFL
item.description: Jalen Hurts has led the Philadelphia Eagles to two Super Bowls, winning the NFL's championship game in 2025 [Getty Images] News that Jalen Hurts played a game hours after being diagnosed with a blood clot had already shocked the NFL world. The Philadelphia Eagles then said their star quarterback will probably miss the rest of the season after multiple blood clots were found in his lungs - a life-threatening condition if not treated quickly. It raised questions over the NFL's handling of the matter and its general approach to player health and safety, partly because the game in question was part of the league's international series. Hurts' initial diagnosis was in London, before the Eagles played at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on 11 October, and he flew back with the team that evening. What do we know about what happened? Why was Hurts allowed to play and then fly home straight after? And what does it mean for him, the Eagles and the NFL? What happened? Sunday, 4 October: Another player stepped on Hurts' left calf during Philadelphia's defeat by the Los Angeles Rams, although he completed the game. Thursday, 8 October: Hurts first reported an issue to the team. He trained in full all week and had treatment on Thursday and Friday. Saturday, 10 October: The Eagles arrived in London in the morning and Hurts visited the Cleveland Clinic that evening. An ultrasound showed he had a superficial blood clot (vein thrombosis) in his calf but he was cleared to play on Sunday. Sunday, 11 October: Hurts returned to the team hotel at about 3am before playing the full game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. A follow-up ultrasound was recommended within 72 hours and Hurts was cleared for the flight home. Wednesday, 14 October: After receiving daily treatment, Hurts had another ultrasound, which showed the clot had moved, and he was ruled out of the next game. Monday, 19 October: Joint statement by the Eagles and Hurts' agent said further tests showed he now has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli (multiple blood clots in both lungs). His treatment will involve blood-thinning medicine and he should make a full recovery but is expected to miss the rest of the season. Hurts threw for 220 yards and a touchdown, but had just two carries for two yards, as the Jaguars claimed a last-gasp 19-17 win in London [Getty Images] What has the NFL said? Some of the initial reports said that Hurts did not sleep for 36 hours before playing in London, but his agent later confirmed that he slept after returning to the hotel and also at the stadium. Dr Allen Sills, the NFL's chief medical officer, was in London that weekend and arranged for Hurts to be evaluated at the Cleveland Clinic, an American-owned private hospital which is an official supplier of sports medicine services for the NFL's London games. item.title: Brewers’ Joey Ortiz speaks up after brutal World Series Game 4 error
item.description: Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Brewers’ Joey Ortiz speaks up after brutal World Series Game 4 error appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Milwaukee Brewers entered the bottom of the 12th inning of Game 4 of the World Series in need of just three more outs to crown themselves champion after Cooper Pratt gave them the lead with a solo shot in the previous half-inning. The Brewers no longer had their best relievers available, with Aaron Ashby and Trevor Megill having appeared earlier in the game, so it was up to Shane Drohan to seal the deal and complete the sweep over the Tampa Bay Rays. And in the first at-bat of the inning, it looked like Drohan had done his job, as he forced a groundball off of Junior Caminero. Alas, third baseman Joey Ortiz made an errant throw to first base, and Jake Bauers was unable to pick up the one-hop throw. The floodgates would then open up for the Rays, as they would record four consecutive hits against Drohan to turn the game on its head and pick up a 4-3 win in walk-off fashion. Joey Ortiz bounces a throw that Jake Bauers couldn't scoop to begin the bottom of the 12th inning pic.twitter.com/jwjqSaBMw9 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Talkin' Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) October 28, 2026 This was a monumental error for Ortiz to make, and at the worst possible time, no less. And while the Brewers aren’t playing the blame game, Ortiz is making no excuses for that major blunder. “Yeah, [they’ve been giving me] encouraging words. But, I mean, it is what it is. I got to make that play. There’s no excuse about it, no matter what anyone says,” Ortiz told reporters after the game, via FOX Sports MLB on X. Joey Ortiz reflects on the costly error in the Brewers' Game 4 loss pic.twitter.com/mRMr9TLzhu — FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 28, 2026 Ortiz is typically surehanded on the field; he did have 10 errors in the regular season, splitting most of his time between third base and shortstop, but the Brewers trust him to make that routine play. Nonetheless, this is just one loss for Milwaukee. They are still in command of the World Series, being up 3-1, and with ace Jacob Misiorowski on the mound for Game 5, the odds are still heavily in their favor. item.title: VIDEO: Hero's welcome! Harry Kane returns to Bayern Munich training after historic 2026 Ballon d'Or victory
item.description: FC Bayern München v Arsenal FC - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport Harry Kane has returned to Bayern Munich's Sabener Strasse training base to a rapturous reception after his historic crowning as the world's best player. The England captain made history in London by becoming the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or in a quarter of a century. A royal reception in Bavaria Upon arriving at the club's facilities on Tuesday, the 33-year-old was greeted by a guard of honour formed by staff members. The forward walked out to the training pitch to rapturous chants of his name, marking a joyous return to domestic duties. Kane’s triumph in London secured Bayern’s first Golden Ball since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981, and the first for any German club since 1996. He is the fourth player in the Bavarian giants' history to claim the prestigious accolade, joining Rummenigge, Franz Beckenbauer, and Gerd Muller. It also finally brings the prize back to Munich after Robert Lewandowski was heavily favoured to win in 2020 before the award was cancelled due to the pandemic. Watch the clip View this post on Instagram Freund leads the tributes Sporting director Christoph Freund was quick to heap praise on the club's talisman, highlighting both his on-pitch brilliance and leadership qualities. "We're all delighted with Harry Kane's performance," Freund stated. "It's not just his goals that make him an exceptional footballer, and it's not just on the pitch that he's a special character." Freund further cemented Kane's growing legacy, adding: "Harry is a great guy, you very rarely come across someone like him, world-class yet so down-to-earth. Harry has taken the centre-forward role to a whole new level - he's an inspiration, especially for young players. He's undoubtedly one of the greatest in football history." The man himself took to social media to reflect on his crowning achievement, expressing gratitude to his club, international colleagues, and supporters. "Where do I begin? That was an evening I'll never forget," Kane posted. "This will live long in the memory." While Kane's individual success brings huge celebration, it arrives during a sombre period for the Bundesliga heavyweights. Head coach Vincent Kompany is currently undergoing medical treatment following a sudden collapse at training last week, while midfielder Joshua Kimmich has taken a leave of absence due to a family bereavement . Assistant coach Aaron Danks reflected on the sharp contrast in emotions around the camp. "You see the extremes that life has to offer," Danks explained. item.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson and Ishan Kishan: How can India fit all four star batsmen in their T20I XI?
item.description: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson and Ishan Kishan: How can India fit all four star batsmen in their T20I XI? originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: India must find room for four star batters once Ishan Kishan returns from injury. Left-hand heavy options and a squeezed middle order make every combination carry a risk. Let's take a look at how Gautam Gambhir can fit all four in the top four, with Nitish at number six. Vaibhav, Abhishek, Sanju, Ishan together in India T20I XI: Batting order combinations, roles and feasibility India have a problem that most teams would love to have, because four of the most destructive young batters in the country are all pushing for the same few spots at the top of the T20I order. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson and Ishan Kishan have each shown that they can win a game inside six overs, and the real question for the team management is how to play all of them in one XI without wrecking the balance of the side. The first thing to understand is that all four of these players do their best work in the same phase of the game. They want the hard new ball, they want the field up, and they want to take the match away from the opposition early. That is wonderful for a side that wants to score 70 or more in the powerplay, but it leaves very little room for anyone who is meant to bat later in the innings. Abhishek, Sooryavanshi and Kishan are all explosive left-handers, so Samson is the only right-hander in the group. A smart opposition captain can use that against India by opening the bowling with a quality off-spinner and keeping him on while the left-handers are at the crease. The squeeze on the rest of the XI is the third issue. Fitting four front-line top-order batters into the first four slots means that finishers, all-rounders and middle-order anchors have to move down or sit out. Axar Patel, Tilak Varma and Shreyas Iyer are all affected by this, and so is Nitish Kumar Reddy. For the purposes of this piece, Hardik Pandya is out of the question because of his injury, and Nitish is the man who steps into that all-rounder slot. He gives India a right-handed finisher and a seam-bowling option, so he is a fixture in every combination discussed below. The recent series gives us a good picture of how flexible the batting order has already become. In the first T20I, Samson and Abhishek opened the innings, and Kishan came in at number three. Samson set the tone in a chase of 226, smashing 67 off 33 balls and winning the Player of the Match award. Kishan then picked up an injury and missed the second game. item.title: There looks to be a striker that Manchester City could target to take the pressure off Erling Haaland
item.description: There looks to be a striker that Manchester City could target to take the pressure off Erling Haaland There is one glaring hole in the current Manchester City squad. Enzo Maresca’s squad does lack up another striker to provide cover for Erling Haaland. In an ideal world, City would sign a quality striker to provide adequate cover and support for their star striker . Enzo Maresca does have options to use if Haaland misses match. Antoine Semenyo and Phil Foden can play the striker role albeit in completely different ways. Floyd Samba has also played up front for City twice this season. However, it does seem that Manchester City would benefit from signing another striker during the January transfer window. It has been reported that Manchester City have now sent scouts to watch Nicolo Tresoldi play for Club Brugge. The highly rated young striker has impressed so far this season. Tresoldi could be the ideal player to provide cover for Erling Haaland if it is a move City want to pursue in a couple of months’ time. Manchester City are amongst a host of clubs who are keeping an eye on Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi. Graeme Bailey has reported for TeamTalk that Manchester City and a host of other Premier League clubs recently had scouts in attendance to watch Nicolo Tresoldi in action for Club Brugge. Tresoldi bagged a hat trick as he fired his team to a 3-2 win over Sint-Truidense . As per Bailey’s report Manchester City, Chelsea, Arsenal, Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United all had scouts at the match. It is also reported by Bailey that Manchester City are carrying out their own ‘due diligence’ by having scouts cast their eye on Nicolo Tresoldi. Furthermore, Bailey reports that City are keeping an eye on promising young players as part of their recruitment strategy. Nicolo Tresoldi ticks all of the right boxes to fill a hole in Enzo Maresca’s squad. First of all, to address the elephant in the room. Manchester City have operated under the philosophy of business as usual during the 115-saga. There is no reason to expect this to change during the January transfer window while that issue remains ongoing. That is the point of view I’m taking when assessing what business Manchester City may do in January. Back to the point at hand. When looking at what type of striker Manchester City could target to be a backup to Erling Haaland, they could target an experienced striker. But that isn’t typically how City operate. The other option is to sign a young striker who could play a role now and potentially have resale value in the future. That is where Nicolo Tresoldi fits. Nicolo Tresoldi is 22 years of age with his best football ahead of him. So far this season he has scored 12 goals in 14 matches in all competitions for Club Brugge. item.description: Louie Hennessey and Kane James have both won their first Wales caps in 2026 [Shutterstock] Established internationals Jac Morgan, Dewi Lake and Aaron Wainwright have hit the ground running after summer moves to England, but a pair of Prem prospects are looking to make an impression as they come back to Wales. Exeter back-row forward Kane James and Bath centre Louie Hennessey are currently with their clubs after spending the start of the week in the Wales camp. The one-cappers are in a 14-strong contingent in Steve Tandy's squad for the Nations Championship who are employed in England. While Morgan, Lake, Wainwright, Tomos Williams and Nicky Smith moved over the border as seasoned Test players, James and Hennessey have earned international chances as Cardiff boys who have been developed in England. The pair will return to Wales next week with the aim of winning caps against Japan, New Zealand, Australia and another southern hemisphere opponent. They also know they have their work cut out against strong competition. Wales call up in-form Page after Dyer injury blow Where are Wales internationals really made? James is fighting for a spot in Wales' strongest department, with Morgan and Wainwright nailed-on starters against Japan, fitness permitting. James Botham, Alex Mann, Taine Basham and Taine Plumtree are the other contenders as 21-year-old Chiefs flanker James tries to make a mark. "It's pretty stacked. There is good competition but a competitive squad is only going to boost us," said James, who faced Argentina in July. "It's similar at Exeter, we've got one hell of a back-row. Being more involved in the senior squad has helped me improve massively." Wales' riches mean players need a point of difference if they are to make the squad, let alone matchday 23. "I'd like to think that I bring something different with my speed and power," said James. "I just like to get my hands on the ball, use my footwork and pace." The flanker has featured four times in the Prem so far this season and also made a couple of telling contributions off the bench in Exeter's narrow Champions Cup loss at Toulouse. The grounding at Sandy Park - where he combines professional rugby with an accounting and finance degree as a part-time student at Exeter University - has allowed him to chase his dream. James played for England Under-20s and was eligible for New Zealand courtesy of his mother, Audrey, who is from the Pacific island of Niue. "It's always been my dream and passion to play for Wales," said James, who was born in Pembrokeshire but grew up in Cardiff, going to Corpus Christi High School and playing for St Peter's RFC. "I grew up watching the likes of Taulupe Faletau and Sam Warburton play in the back row for Wales. "I was inspired by them, so it was a proud moment to play [against Argentina] and something that I had worked towards for a while." item.title: Value Adder: Why Liverpool refuse to quit on Jarrad Branthwaite
item.description: Value Adder: Why Liverpool refuse to quit on Jarrad Branthwaite Liverpool are refusing to give up on a pursuit of Jarrad Branthwaite. Here's what our Value Adder data model tells us. Liverpool are in need of a centre-back and one name that simply refuses to go away is Jarrad Branthwaite. Even if that name probably should drop off their shortlist, if we’re entirely honest. The centre-back had a difficult season last year, playing just 680 Premier League minutes, but that’s really the least of Liverpool’s concerns. Ultimately, he’s a player they almost certainly cannot sign - Everton won’t let it happen. The Reds haven’t tried to sign someone from Everton for years now, with their last serious attempt being Romelu Lukaku in 2015. That ended as you’d expect - a firm ‘no’, to put it in nicer terms, and that was that. No negotiation, in other words. So why are they actually, per Football Insider , willing to persist with the idea of Branthwaite? We’ve had a look at our Value Adder model to make sense of it. Value Adder: Jarrad Branthwaite Branthwaite is an interesting player. He also carries that precious homegrown status and has several Premier League seasons under his belt. Immediately, he eliminates many of the concerns that clubs have when signing a centre-back. The issue is that his best season happened a few years ago now. It came under Sean Dyche in 2023/24 and Branthwaite has failed to match it since - though, injuries are partly to blame for that. But that’s the campaign that will drive interest in Branthwaite. A feeling among clubs that here’s a player who is undervalued based on his current form if you can get him back to that top level. Our Value Adder model has Branthwaite ranked as the no.6 most valuable centre-back in the Premier League for 2023/24. That dropped to 17th for 2024/25, as both his per-90 and per-action value fell. That, though, was largely because his on-ball influence fell off a cliff while he provided 0 goals compared to 3 in his best season. Branthwaite’s defensive numbers remained solid and we had him down as roughly the same value per-90 defensively for all of 2023/24, 2024/25 and 2025/26. That does suggest that Branthwaite is still the same player as he was in 2023/24 - it’s a shift in Everton that perhaps doesn’t allow for him to play much of a role that sees his overall value fall. The player was never a massive passer but he dropped into an outlier for passes in 2024/25, sitting over one standard deviation below average for attempted, successful and key passes per 90. In fact, his weighted attacking actions are all the way down in the 13th percentile for centre-backs. This wasn’t the case the year before, with Branthwaite showing a much brighter all-around game. item.description: Arsenal's 16-year-old winger Max Dowman was sent off for the first time in his senior career [Getty Images] Max Dowman is used to grabbing headlines for producing moments of magic but, after being sent off in just his second start of the season as Arsenal suffered a shock loss to Fleetwood Town, the 16-year-old is facing the first test of his short career. item.title: Manchester City could solve two problems at once with one clever selection decision
item.description: Manchester City could solve two problems at once with one clever selection decision It isn’t a stretch to say that Marc Guehi has been below his best in recent matches. Three of the four goals that Manchester City have conceded against Ipswich Town and Aston Villa have come via mistakes from the England international. Guehi does look like he is in need of a rest. To start this season, Enzo Maresca has preferred to partner Ruben Dias and Guehi in the heart of City’s defence. With Guehi being down on form there is a simple solution on offer for Enzo Maresca to use to give Guehi a break and keep the heart of Manchester City’s in strong shape. It is time for Abdukodir Khusanov to move back to centre-back for Manchester City. There looks to be one simple move for Enzo Maresca to make to give Marc Guehi a much-needed break. That is moving Abdukodir Khusanov back to his natural position at centre-back. For the majority of this season Khusanov has played at right-back. The Uzbekistan international has been serviceable at right-back but that isn’t his natural position. Khusanov thrives at centre-back and his pace and strength in a challenge does add a different dimension to the Manchester City defence. Shifting Khusanov across will help Guehi get rest as he does look fatigued and also keep Ruben Dias at the back. The variable in this equation is the situation at right-back for Enzo Maresca’s side. Matheus Nunes has recently been injured. Nunes’ injury has forced Khusanov to be deployed at right-back. If Nunes is fit, Khusanov could easily slot back into his natural role. Enzo Maresca could even start Rico Lewis at right-back if need be. Lewis may not be suited to playing right-back in the Premier League due to the pace and power that many wingers in England’s top flight possess. But it is an option available to Enzo Maresca to give Guehi a rest and allow Khusanov to play the role that best suits him and his team. There is also another option for Enzo Maresca to consider. The same option also exists at left-back for Enzo Maresca to consider. Josko Gvardiol could shift to centre-back with Nico O’Reilly starting at left-back. Provided, of course, that Nico O’Reilly is fit. O’Reilly has been suffering from a back injury. That option is there for Enzo Maresca to pursue. Either way, there is a way for Maresca to rest Guehi and keep the heart of the Manchester City defence strong. A shift at either full-back position is an option for Enzo Maresca to consider. Marc Guehi needs a rest. His recent displays indicate this. The number one option would be to get Abdukodir Khusanov alongside Ruben Dias. Playing at centre-back is where Khusanov does his best work. If that isn’t an option, Josko Gvardiol could also make the shift across. Either way the option is there for Enzo Maresca. You do feel that it needs to be considered to give Marc Guehi a break.

The England captain made history in London on Monday night, and the UK Government has now addressed the growing calls for the striker to be knighted. Calls grow for Kane's ultimate royal honour The Bayern Munich striker claimed football's top individual prize at a lavish London ceremony, edging out fierce competition from Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. In doing so, he became the first Englishman to lift the Golden Ball in a quarter of a century, fittingly achieving the feat exactly 70 years after Sir Stanley Matthews secured the inaugural award. Following this milestone, Labour MPs Rosena Allin-Khan and Clive Efford publicly backed the Three Lions captain for a knighthood once his playing days conclude. Downing Street responds to knighthood speculation Addressing the media, a spokeswoman for Prime Minister Andy Burnham praised the forward's monumental achievement while remaining coy on the prospect of a royal title. She noted that the highest levels of government are acutely aware of his impact on the domestic game. "Yes, the PM would like to congratulate Harry Kane on winning the Ballon d'Or," the spokeswoman stated. "To be the first Englishman to win it in 25 years is an extraordinary achievement, and what a moment to do it here at home, 70 years after Sir Stanley Matthews won the inaugural award." She added: "It caps a remarkable season and Harry continues to set a brilliant example to young players across the country, and the PM knows the whole nation will be incredibly proud of him. item.title: Luka Doncic’s 41-point masterpiece not enough as Lakers fall to Trail Blazers
item.description: Through the early parts of 2026-27, the Lakers had cobbled together enough strong defensive moments that allowed their league-best offense to carry them to three straight wins. Those moments didn’t come often enough against the Trail Blazers Tuesday night at Crypto.com Arena, leading to the Lakers losing their first game of the season. Despite Luka Doncic picking up where he left off after 52 points in Salt Lake City on Sunday, the Lakers didn’t have the defensive support behind another brilliant offensive performance, falling to the Blazers 136-129 to drop to 3-1 on the season. Luka Doncic reacts to a Lakers foul during the first half of the Lakers’ 136-129 loss to the Trail Blazers on Oct. 27, 2026 at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. Austin Reaves was once again uber-efficient, recording 26 points on 8-of-13 shooting (4 of 8 on 3s), plus seven assists and four rebounds. Deni Avdija drives to the basket while being guarded by Ziaire Williams (behind) during the first half of the Lakers’ loss to the Trail Blazers. AP Photo/Caroline Brehman But the Blazers, who entered Tuesday with the league’s second-best offense, took advantage of the Lakers’ struggles with containing the ball. The Blazers were led by Deni Avdija’s 23 points, nine assists and four rebounds. Ja Morant (23 points, four assists), Damian Lillard (21 points, four assists) and Jrue Holiday (22 points, four rebounds) also scored at least 20 points for the Blazers. Luka Doncic, who scored 41 points, shoots a long jumper over Sidy Cissoko during the Lakers’ loss to the Trail Blazers. item.title: Vance aiming for a more attacking Guernsey FC
item.description: Record goalscorer Ross Allen (left) has scored three times for Guernsey FC this season [Fran Torode] Tony Vance says he is adopting a more aggressive style of play now that Guernsey FC have seen many of their injured players return. The Green Lions were without the likes of Sam Murray, Ross Allen, Fin Du Port and Charlton Gauvain earlier this season, but all apart from Gauvain are now back. It has led to an upturn in fortunes, with Guernsey winning their last four matches and moving up to seventh place in the Southern Combination Premier Division. "We started off the season with a plan and it was working until we got players injured," the Guernsey FC manager told BBC Radio Guernsey. "Now it's given me a time to reflect and look at it and think now we've got our resources back, we're playing a little bit of catch up so maybe we can go a little bit more aggressive than we were planning on doing. "Obviously you've got to take each game as it comes and see how you go, but ultimately from our point of view, we're attacking games now and we've got to try and get as many points as we can." Guernsey FC promotion hopes crushed in play-off final loss Guernsey are seventh having won seven of their 12 matches but they are 12 points off league leaders Haywards Heath Town, although have two games in hand. The islanders missed out on promotion back to the Isthmian League last season when they were beaten by Peacehaven and Telscombe in the play-off final in May. Vance feels that the play-offs will again be his side's best hope of returning to the eighth tier having been relegated in April 2025. "We're never going to have enough to win the league," Vance added. "Haywards Heath and all these other teams have got far more resources than us, they don't have to travel, so it's going to take something really special to win the league. "We're always going to have those challenges, so probably the play-offs is the most realistic thing. "Obviously, if we manage to really have a massive spout and huge form and the others drop, then of course we'd keep going, but I just don't think we've quite got enough really given the logistical problems to go and win the league, so maybe it's the play-offs." item.title: Jacob Misiorowski to start World Series Game 5 after Brewers fail to sweep Rays
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL – After starting the first game in each of the Milwaukee Brewers ’ three playoff series, Jacob Misiorowski also will start what they hope to be their final game of 2026. A 12-inning, 4-3 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays kept the Brewers from a World Series sweep, but they’ll have their ace on the mound for Game 5 on Oct. 28 at Tropicana Field. “It’s all hands on deck,” Brewers manager Pat Murphy said of having the likely National League Cy Young Award winner ready to go. “You can write it up and hope that they perform like the back of their baseball card, but that doesn’t always happen. You go with what you believe is the deal. I trust our guys. … They put themselves in a position to win” Milwaukee did that in Game 4 when rookie Cooper Pratt homered to lead off the 12 th inning, but then Antonio Senzatela and Shane Drohan failed to get an out in the bottom of the 12th. After taking it easy on their bullpen in a 10-1 victory a night earlier, the Brewers ran through seven relievers in a game that was tied for six innings before Pratt’s homer. Although Misiorowski was in the bullpen, Murphy said he didn’t entertain the thought of using him once the Brewers took the lead. “You can’t blow that type of situation on a one-run lead on the road,” he said. “If we were in the 13th inning and we had a three-run lead, that might have been a little bit different. Probably still wouldn’t have.” The Rays benefited from an inning-opening error on third baseman Joey Ortiz, who failed to throw out Junior Caminero on a ground ball against the right-hander Senzatela, who’d come into the game in the 11th, and then three singles off the lefty Drohan. “I was playing it by ear, ready for whatever they needed,” Misiorowski said. “It’s the World Series.” Misiorowski went 16-5 in the regular season with a 1.80 ERA but has found the playoffs a bit more of a grind. His victory in Game 1 of the World Series marked the first time he made it through five innings as the San Diego Padres in the NLDS, the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS and then the Rays all were able to run up his pitch counts early. In 13⅓ innings in the playoffs Misiorowski has given up 13 hits and six earned runs, as well as five walks. He struck out six in four innings against the Padres, five in 4⅓ against the Dodgers and three in five innings against the Rays to start the World Series. As a rookie in 2025, Misiorowski went 2-1 in the playoffs, winning two relief appearances and then taking the loss in his start in Game 3 of the NLCS against the Dodgers. The 24-year-old right-hander has pitched nearly three times as many innings in 2026 as he did in ’25. Although Misiorowski has shown some fatigue, he still threw 40 of his 78 pitches at or above 100 mph in Game 1. Asked for seeing a playoff opponent a second time in a series or coming back on four days’ rest, Misiorowski shrugged at the thought. “I’m used to it in the minor leagues, going Tuesday-Sunday, so this isn’t a new phenomenon,” he said.

item.title: Fever Insider Flags Daunting Challenges for Future GM Amid Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell & Aliyah Boston Dilemma
item.description: ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire The 2026 WNBA season proved that the Indiana Fever have the talent to compete for a championship, even though they fell to the Las Vegas Aces in the first round of the playoffs. One of their biggest shortcomings was their defensive struggles, an issue they will need to address next season. Indiana will want to keep its core intact while improving on that weakness, but retaining its foundation could prove just as challenging as strengthening it. With Caitlin Clark, Aliyah Boston and Kelsey Mitchell forming the heart of the franchise, the Fever have an opportunity to remain contenders for years to come. The challenge, though, lies in navigating a delicate financial balancing act that has become even more pressing as Indiana undergoes a major front-office shake-up. Team president Kelly Krauskopf stepped down on October 23, while general manager Amber Cox was fired later that same day, leaving the franchise searching for new leadership ahead of a crucial offseason. The incoming GM will inherit a roster with three key players whose futures come with significant financial considerations, making the task of keeping Indiana’s core together a major priority. So Fever insider Chloe Peterson has now highlighted the daunting challenges awaiting the franchise’s next leader. “With the Fever’s championship window in full bloom, they need someone in the front office who will be able to take advantage of that. Indiana’s new GM should be someone who can, above all, navigate this salary cap situation they’re in,” Peterson said, as per an X post by IndyStar . “Aliyah Boston will make a supermax, which is 20% of the team’s salary cap, in 2027, and Caitlin Clark is eligible for a raise up to 17% of the team’s salary cap. Add in potentially re-signing Kelsey Mitchell, and they’re running out of space already. This new GM needs to figure out how to make it all work, either through trades, the draft, or smart free agency moves, including if they themselves want to retain Mitchell for 2027.” “The new GM also needs to have a form of thick skin. There is a microscope around the Fever, especially, and that comes with more fans, detractors, and trolls. This new GM will need to be able to detach from that social media slop while also knowing how to maneuver the perception the Fever have built around the league. item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL – Joey Ortiz was as good as it gets defensively in the regular season for the Milwaukee Brewers . He accounted for 16 outs above average between third base and shortstop, ninth-best in the major leagues, along with eight defensive runs saved. The glove work was a saving grace for the 28-year-old as he battled through a miserable first half at the plate before posting a resurgent final few months. Injuries hampered Ortiz down the stretch, however, and with David Hamilton swinging a hot bat from the outset of the postseason, Ortiz has largely found himself on the outside looking in as the Brewers have marched their way to within a victory of their first World Series championship. It was against that backdrop that Ortiz was inserted into Game 4 in the ninth inning with Milwaukee tied, 2-2, with the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on Tuesday night, Oct. 27. Taking over at third base after Andrew Vaughn pinch-hit for Hamilton, Ortiz twice bounced throws over to first baseman Jake Bauers on routine ground balls. The first time, two batters into his appearance, Ortiz had his bacon saved by a great pick by Bauers on a short hop. The second time, with Junior Caminero leading off the bottom of the 12th inning after Cooper Pratt's home run had given Milwaukee a one-run lead and three outs to get before popping champagne bottles, Ortiz wasn't so lucky. And not long thereafter the Brewers were on the wrong end of an absolutely brutal 4-3 loss that will now necessitate a Game 5 on Wednesday, Oct. 28. Antonio Senzatela, on the mound for the righty-righty matchup against Caminero, came up and in on his third pitch and broke the slugger's bat with a sinker. The ball was pulled down the line and Ortiz, stationed near the third-base line and about a step in front of the outfield grass, fielded the ball with a backhand. He had plenty of time to gather himself and make a strong throw to first with Caminero a slow runner. Instead, he quickly fired over and the ball bounced a few feet in front of Bauers, who was at least able to keep the ball in front of him as Caminero crossed the bag. "I fielded the ball and I think I should have took another couple more steps toward first," Ortiz said afterward. "I made a [expletive] throw." Added Bauers: "A little in-between pick, didn't come up with it. Sometimes you get 'em, sometimes you don't." item.description: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Islanders defenseman Matthew Schaefer pulls off historic OT feat in win vs. Predators appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . New York Islanders defenseman Matthew Schaefer made NHL history in Tuesday night’s 4-3 shootout win over the Nashville Predators. The 19-year-old played every second of the five-minute overtime period, becoming the first player to accomplish the feat since official real-time ice-time tracking began in the 2009-10 season. Schaefer drew a tripping penalty against Nashville forward Filip Forsberg during overtime, creating an opportunity for a short rest during the ensuing stoppage. However, New York kept its young defenseman on the ice throughout the resulting four-on-three power play. He remained in action for the final 43 seconds after the advantage expired, completing the entire overtime period without a shift change. The Hamilton, Ontario, native also had to prevent a potential breakaway by Forsberg after leaving the penalty box. His demanding performance resulted in a career-high 32 minutes and 16 seconds of ice time, more than six minutes above the next-highest total among Islanders skaters. His workload was also the third-highest recorded by any NHL player in a game this season. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Schaefer contributed an assist in the victory, extending his point streak to five consecutive games. He now has two goals and nine assists for 11 points through 12 appearances in his second NHL season. His average ice time stands at 26 minutes and 43 seconds per game, ranking fourth across the league. Schaefer earned the Calder Trophy unanimously last season after finishing with 23 goals and 36 assists for 59 points across all 82 games. New York initially built a three-goal advantage through Bo Horvat, Anthony Duclair and Brayden Schenn. However, Forsberg, Alexander Kerfoot and Ryan O’Reilly scored for the Predators to force overtime. Kyle Palmieri and Horvat then converted their shootout attempts to secure the result, giving goaltender Semyon Varlamov his first win in nearly two years. The Islanders sit fourth in the Metropolitan Division with 14 points from 12 games. They will conclude their three-game road trip versus the Minnesota Wild on Thursday night before beginning a three-game homestand against the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday.
